findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator breaks on datetime keys used by the audit log endpoint
findings.body:
`OptimizedCursorPaginator` copies the integer `Paginator` key logic: `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on `getattr(item, self.key)`, and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw cursor value.

The audit log endpoint uses it with `order_by="-datetime"`, so the value is a `datetime`. `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError` as soon as `build_cursor` computes next/prev values, so any request with `optimized_pagination=true` and at least one result returns a 500.

Even with that fixed, a cursor value would be a millisecond integer compared directly against a timestamp column in the `extra(where=...)` clause, which is a type mismatch. It should subclass or reuse `DateTimePaginator`'s key and cursor conversion.

findings.title: Negative offsets passed to queryset slicing crash the request
findings.body:
When `enable_advanced_features` is on and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code slices the QuerySet with a negative start (`queryset[start_offset:stop]`). Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise `ValueError`/`AssertionError`, so a user-controlled cursor like `0:-5:0` turns into a 500.

The comment says "the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically", which is false.

The same applies to `BasePaginator.get_result` (line 182): for `is_prev` cursors the offset is passed through unclamped. Negative offsets should be rejected with `BadPaginationError`.

findings.title: AttributeError when member is None; weak gate for advanced pagination
findings.body:
`organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated whenever the user is not a superuser. `organization_context.member` can be None (for example staff or API-token access without a membership), which raises `AttributeError` and returns a 500.

It is also evaluated even when `optimized_pagination` was not requested, so these requests fail on the default path too.

Separately, `has_global_access` is true for every member of an org with open membership. That is not an "authorized administrators" check, so the experimental negative-offset path is exposed far more widely than intended.

findings.title: Missing end_timestamp_precise crashes the consumer batch
findings.body:
`val["end_timestamp_precise"]` is accessed with a hard index. Any span payload that lacks this field raises `KeyError` inside `process_batch`, which fails the whole batch and can wedge the consumer on a poison message.

Use `.get()` with a fallback, or validate the field and drop or log invalid spans.

findings.title: Hardcoded 1000-span cap ignores configuration and drops spans silently
findings.body:
The eviction limit is hardcoded to 1000 in Lua. Meanwhile the Python-side `max_segment_spans` check was removed, so the `max_segment_spans` constructor parameter is now dead configuration.

`zpopmin` silently discards the earliest-ending spans with no metric or log. This replaces the previous `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric and error log.

The redirect-map entries for evicted spans also stay in `span-buf:sr:*` until TTL, because `done_flush_segments` only hdel's the spans that were actually flushed. Pass the limit as an ARGV and emit a metric when eviction happens.

findings.title: Redirect depth limit reduced 10x without explanation
findings.body:
The redirect loop bound was reduced from 10000 to 1000, and the comment explaining the consequence was removed. Segment trees deeper than 1000 levels will now fail to join correctly into a single segment.

This behavior change is unrelated to the stated eviction optimization and is undocumented.
